why: The Registry pages the whole paperbook as one sequence. A break, repeat or reversal in the printed page numbers means the bench cannot be taken to a page by number, and the filing comes back.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Repaginate the bundle as one continuous sequence and re-stamp every page. PARAM can do this and regenerate the index to match.

text: English Translation of Vernacular be filed.
why: Proceedings in the High Court of Delhi are in English. Any document in Hindi or another language must be accompanied by a typed English translation, or it cannot be read on the record.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: File a typed English translation of each vernacular page, certified by the advocate. PARAM lists the exact page ranges that need it.

text: Margin of 4 cm. be kept on the left side of the annexures.
why: The left margin is where the paperbook is bound and where the Registry stamps. Text running into it is physically lost after binding.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Re-typeset or re-scan the flagged pages with a 4 cm left margin before filing.

text: Fair typed copies of dim annexures be filed.
why: A faint photocopy or low-resolution scan is treated as illegible. The Registry requires a fair typed copy alongside it.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: File a fair typed copy of each dim page, marked as the typed copy of that annexure.

why: An unattested affidavit is not a sworn statement. The supporting affidavit must carry the deponent's signature and the attestation of the Oath Commissioner or Notary.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Have the affidavit sworn and attested before an Oath Commissioner or Notary, and file the attested copy.

text: Petition / appeal be stamped / signed by the Counsel.
why: The petition must carry counsel's signature and stamp. An unsigned petition is not a valid presentation.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Sign and affix counsel's stamp at the foot of the petition before filing.

why: Without a vakalatnama on record the advocate has no authority to appear, and the matter cannot be entertained.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Execute and file the vakalatnama, signed by the client and accepted by the advocate.

text: Welfare stamp of Rs. 10/- be affixed.
why: The Advocates' Welfare Fund stamp is required on the vakalatnama. Its absence is one of the most routine objections raised.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Affix the Rs.10 Advocates' Welfare Fund stamp on the vakalatnama and cancel it as required.

text: Memo of parties be filed duly signed.
why: The memo of parties fixes the array of parties and their addresses for service. The Registry will not number a matter without it.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: PARAM can generate a memo of parties from the cause title for you to check and sign.

text: List of Dates and synopsis should be filed.
why: The synopsis and chronological list of dates is how the bench reads the matter first. It is a mandatory part of the paperbook.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Prepare a synopsis with a chronological list of dates and events up to the impugned order.

text: Listing proforma duly filled in should be filed, both sets.
why: The listing proforma drives how the matter is categorised and listed. Filings routinely bounce on this alone.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: PARAM can generate a listing proforma skeleton from the bundle for you to complete.

text: Certified copy of impugned order be given.
why: An appeal or revision cannot be entertained without the certified copy of the order challenged, and its dates are what drive the s.12(2) limitation exclusion.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Apply for and file the certified copy of the impugned order. Keep the application and delivery dates, PARAM uses them for s.12(2).

text: All papers be filed on foolscap papers / on one side of the papers.
why: The paperbook is prepared single-sided on standard paper so it can be bound and annotated. Mixed page sizes in one bundle indicate a violation.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Reprint or re-scan so every page is the same size and printed on one side only.

text: Correct and relevant provision of law be given.
why: A petition invoking the wrong provision (Art. 226 where Art. 227 lies, or the wrong section of the governing Act) is returned to be corrected.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Check the provision in the cause title and prayer against the relief actually sought.

text: Appeal / petition is barred by time.
why: Section 3 of the Limitation Act is mandatory: a court must dismiss a time-barred proceeding even if no party raises limitation. A filing that sits in defect while limitation runs can become unfilable.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections (CRLR)

fix.guidance: File an application under s.5 of the Limitation Act explaining every single day of delay. PARAM can draft one with a day-by-day chart.

text: Annexure be stamped @ 65 paisa per 360 words.
why: Annexures attract stamp at the prescribed rate. PARAM cannot see the physical stamps on a scan, so this is surfaced as a reminder, not a finding.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Verify the stamp affixed on each annexure against the prescribed rate before filing.

text: Caveat report is to be obtained at the time of each subsequent filing.
why: A caveat lodged by the opposite side must be checked at every fresh filing. This is a Registry step PARAM cannot perform for you.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: Obtain a fresh caveat report from the Registry before presenting the filing.

text: Notice of Motion with proof of service effected upon Respondent be filed.
why: Where advance service is required, proof of service must accompany the filing.
source: High Court of Delhi — List of Common Objections

fix.guidance: File the notice of motion together with proof of advance service on the respondent.
